title: Harlow Street bathroom refit, delivered
content: The Harlow Street bathroom went in this week. Painted shaker fronts, brass pulls, and a vanity that had to clear a heating pipe nobody had drawn. It did. #BrightsideBuilt

title: Why solid-wood doors move with the seasons
content: A door that sticks in August and rattles in January is not a defect. Wood takes on moisture and lets it go. Here is what to adjust, and what to leave alone. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare

title: Saturday at the bench
content: Saturday in the shop. Two doors hung, one coffee gone cold, and the showroom open until two. Come by. #BrightsideBuilt #ShopLife

title: Three signs your drawer slides are done
content: A drawer that drops when it opens, a slide that squeals, a runner that has gone shiny on one side. Any one of these and the slide is finished, not the drawer. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare

title: Summer showroom hours
content: Summer hours start this week: Tuesday to Friday nine to five, Saturday nine to two. Bring a door if you want to see a pull against it. #BrightsideBuilt

title: How a door gets finished here, in four passes
content: Four passes: a sanding sealer, a sand by hand, the first lacquer coat, a second sand, the final coat. The sand between coats is the step people skip and the reason our doors feel the way they do. #BrightsideBuilt

title: Lacquer or oil: which finish survives a working kitchen
content: Lacquer gives you a hard shell that wipes clean and chips if you hit it. Oil gives you a soft surface that scratches and repairs with a rag. Neither is wrong; pick the one you will live with. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare

title: Meet Tomas, our finishing lead
content: Tomas has sprayed every door that left this shop for six years. Ask him about lacquer and clear an afternoon. #BrightsideBuilt #ShopLife

title: The hinge, not the door: which screw fixes a droop
content: A cabinet door that droops on one side is nearly always a hinge, not the door. One screwdriver, two adjustment screws, five minutes. Here is which screw does what. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare

title: Fall hardware run opens for pre-order
content: The fall hardware run is open for pre-order: aged brass, matte black, and the bronze. Trade accounts get first call on quantities. Link below. #BrightsideBuilt

title: Soft-close hinges fail one way, and it is not the spring
content: When a soft-close door starts slamming, the spring is fine. The damper, the small piston at the hinge cup, has lost its oil. Swap the damper before you swap the hinge. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare

title: What the award judges wrote about the inset doors
content: The judges called the inset doors on the Pine Street kitchen the tightest tolerances in the category. The family called them the doors that finally close. Both are true. #BrightsideBuilt

title: A thank-you to the trade school class
content: Twenty-two students spent Thursday in the finishing booth asking why we sand between coats. The answer is the next post. Thank you for the questions. #BrightsideBuilt #ShopLife

title: Brass pulls: clean them without stripping the patina
content: Warm water, a drop of dish soap, a soft cloth. That is the whole method for brass pulls. The bottle under the sink takes the patina off in one wipe and it does not come back. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare

title: Inset versus overlay doors, in one picture
content: Inset or overlay? Inset sits inside the frame and costs you tolerance; overlay sits on the frame and forgives a wall that is not square. One picture, both answers. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare

title: Ridgeway kitchen: eleven weeks from template to install
content: Ridgeway went from template to install in eleven weeks, with a range hood that changed size twice. The cabinets did not. Before and after in the frames. #BrightsideBuilt

title: Two showroom slots open for August consults
content: Two consult slots are open in August for kitchens starting this fall. Call the shop and ask for Dana. #BrightsideBuilt

title: The bench on a Saturday, part two
content: Saturday again. The showroom is open, the second bench is hanging doors, and the coffee is fresh for once. Come and ask us anything about your kitchen. #BrightsideBuilt #ShopLife

title: Why we sand between coats
content: The trade school class asked why we sand between coats. Because the first coat raises the grain, and a second coat over raised grain feels like a fence post. Ninety seconds in the booth. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare

title: Press: the county magazine on the workshop
content: The county magazine spent a morning in the shop and wrote about the sanding room. The line we kept: a workshop that measures twice and finishes three times. Link below. #BrightsideBuilt

title: What a cabinet quote should show you, line by line
content: Five lines every cabinet quote should show: box construction, door style, finish system, hardware brand, and who installs. A quote that hides one of them is hiding the price. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare

title: Meet Dana, who answers the phone
content: When you call the shop you get Dana, who has taken every order here for four years and can tell you which finish you asked for last time before you remember. #BrightsideBuilt #ShopLife

title: Humidity and your cabinets: the August checklist
content: August is when doors stick. Check the gap at the top rail, run the range fan while you cook, and leave the hinge screws alone until October. Four frames, four checks. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare

title: Before and after: the Linden Avenue pantry
content: The Linden Avenue pantry had a chimney breast in the middle of it. The new run wraps it and gains a shelf. Before and after side by side. #BrightsideBuilt

title: September consult calendar opens Monday

title: Soft-close, part two: the damper swap in four photos
content: The damper swap, in four photos: unclip the old piston, note which way the flat side faced, clip the new one on, close the door twice. If it still slams, the hinge cup is bent, not the damper. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare

title: Shop dog, shop rules
content: Biscuit has three rules: no sawdust in the water bowl, no barking at the spray booth, and every visitor gets greeted. Saturday hours as usual. #BrightsideBuilt #ShopLife

title: Seasonal wood movement: what to do before the heat comes on
content: Before the heat comes on, wipe the door edges, check the top-rail gap, and write down which doors stick now. In January the same doors will rattle, and the note tells you nothing moved but the air. #BrightsideBuilt #CabinetCare
